paper-white.$description: Paper White — Page canvas, card base, text on dark cards — the dominant surface

ink-black.$description: Ink Black — Dark borders and separators for elevated surfaces and inverted UI. Do not promote it to the primary CTA color

slate-gray.$description: Slate Gray — Muted text, inactive tags, form labels

stone-border.$description: Stone Border — Hairline borders, dividers, card outlines

mist-gray.$description: Mist Gray — Tertiary text, disabled states

bone.$description: Bone — Soft surface tint, secondary card backgrounds

pale-sage.$description: Pale Sage — Hairline borders, dividers, input outlines, and card edges on light surfaces.

lavender-mist.$description: Lavender Mist — Lavender card variant — secondary project category, tag fills

dusty-rose.$description: Dusty Rose — Red state accent for badges, validation surfaces, and short status labels.

deep-violet.$description: Deep Violet — Violet accent for outlined action borders, linked labels, and lightweight interactive emphasis.

burnt-amber.$description: Burnt Amber — Warm brown border accent on tags and badges — the signature warm neutral that anchors the cool pastels

honey-gold.$description: Honey Gold — Gold accent for tag text, highlighted labels — the single warm highlight color

burgundy.$description: Burgundy — Error/status red — badge backgrounds and warning borders

blush-border.$description: Blush Border — Soft pink border accent for rose-category cards and tags

nng.$description: Primary typeface across all contexts: display headlines (44–69px, weight 300–400), headings (22–29px, weight 500), body (14–18px, weight 400), captions and micro-labels (12–13px, weight 500, uppercase). Custom geometric sans with tight tracking on large sizes (-0.021em at 69px) — the slight negative tracking makes the large display headlines feel dense and poster-like rather than airy.

roboto.$description: Secondary system font used sparingly — likely for rendered user content (descriptions, quotes) where a neutral fallback is needed. Weight 400 only, tight tracking (-0.103em) gives it a condensed feel.

apercu-pro-mono.$description: Monospaced accent — used for code-like or identifier text (project IDs, timestamps). Normal letter-spacing distinguishes it from the proportional Nng.

moderat.$description: Moderat — detected in extracted data but not described by AI
